forecaster_note: Saturday is back-to-front: the swell doesn't turn up until the wind does. Only 67 kJ at dawn and 90 kJ at 10am — genuinely small and weak — then it nearly doubles to 170 kJ by midday and 206 kJ by dark, right as the S cross-shore builds to 9kph gusting 13. Showers on and off all day. Sunday is the session: 239 kJ at 8am and 252 kJ at 10am under a light SE offshore, then it falls off a cliff to 137 kJ by noon. Short 7s spacing keeps Surfline's rating honest at poor–fair, but that is the most energy of the weekend arriving with the best wind of the weekend. — Surf Guru agent summary (Surfline regional forecaster text was unavailable this refresh). Water temp is a NSW-wide station estimate, not a Dee Why reading.

wind.summary: Light SW offshore 3kph at 7am, backing SSW then S cross-shore from about 10am — 6kph gusting 9 mid-morning, 9kph gusting 13 by mid-afternoon. Never strong, but it is on it from 10am just as the swell fills in. Sunday flips to a light SE offshore 3–9kph all day.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW layers (DPI Fisheries + SLSNSW drone) read successfully this refresh, but the most recent detection anywhere in NSW is still dated 25 July — 21 days with nothing published, so no all-clear can be given. The last Northern Beaches entries were Long Reef and Dee Why on 25 July (water evacuated). Tap through and check the live map before you paddle out.

days.label: Today
days.note: A patience day. Dawn is the weakest water of the weekend — 67 kJ at 6am, 79 at 8am, still only 90 by 10am — and the dominant swell is 3.8ft @ 9s from 184°, dead south, the exact angle that goes fat and gutless at Dee Why. The energy more than doubles to 170 kJ by midday, but the S cross-shore arrives on the same schedule and Surfline drops every spot to poor–fair from about 1pm. Showers through the day, 15°C air. Your realistic window is 11am–1pm at Curl Curl or Long Reef on the ramp, and even that is a consolation prize — the real one is tomorrow at 8am.

dee-why.window: 11am–1pm as the energy ramps 90 → 170 kJ, off the 9:57am high. Before 10am there is not enough water moving to bother. Light SW offshore only until about 9am.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point — but 184° is the wrong door
tip.text: This is the swell direction that makes Dee Why look small on a day the buoys look fine. 3.8ft @ 9s at 184° is dead south: it has to bend hard around the headland and arrives fat, walling instead of bowling. The 1.1ft @ 11s at 76° ENE is the only thing in the water pointed at you properly — too small to carry the day, but it is why the odd set will suddenly stand up. Sit wide on the Point, ignore the 5s SE mush, and take the longer-spaced ones for your frontside rights. If you want actual size today, drive to Curl Curl.

alerts: 184° dead south — worst angle for this bank
Only 90 kJ at 10am; the swell arrives with the wind
S cross-shore builds from ~10am, poor–fair from 1pm

long-reef.window: 10am–1pm. The one spot where the S wind reads offshore from 9am onward — same 130 kJ, better wind, half a foot more size than Dee Why.

tip.label: Best wind of the four today
tip.text: The S that turns cross-shore everywhere else comes off the land here from about 9am, so you get the ramping energy with clean faces. 9s spacing is workable but not generous — paddle for the marked sets and let the in-betweens go. It is still only waist-to-shoulder until midday, so bring the volume.

alerts: Small until midday — 90 kJ at 10am
Poor–fair from 1pm as the S builds

curl-curl.window: 11am–1pm. Biggest of the four on this dead-south angle — waist to head while Dee Why is waist to chest — and the S goes offshore here from about 11am.

tip.label: The size play today
tip.text: Identical 130 kJ, and Curl Curl converts it into head-high faces because 184° swings almost straight in rather than wrapping. On 9s spacing the north end usually has the shape and the south corner tends to close out — drive by and look before you wax up. If the sand is wrong, Long Reef is two minutes away with better wind.

alerts: Bank-dependent on short-period south
Closeout risk in the south corner
Poor–fair from 1pm

manly.window: Skip it. Thigh to stomach all morning and Surfline has it dropping to outright poor by 1pm — the only spot of the four to go that far.

tip.label: Backside on the lefts — not on 184°
tip.text: North Steyne is the most shadowed of the four from dead south and the numbers say it flatly: 1–2ft here while Curl Curl runs waist-to-head on identical energy. Nothing wrong with the tide or the wind, there is simply no swell reaching it. Save the backhand for a proper NE–ENE pulse.

alerts: Smallest of the four — fully shadowed from 184°
Rated poor from 1pm

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: This is the weekend. 98 kJ at 6am, 239 kJ by 8am and 252 kJ at 10am — the most energy of the two days — arriving under a light SE offshore of 3–9kph that holds all day. Direction improves too: 5.8ft @ 7s from 143° SE with a 2.3ft @ 17s long-period south underneath, a far better door than today's 184°. The catch is spacing and timing. 7s is windswell-fast, which is why Surfline keeps everything at poor–fair, and the whole thing collapses to 137 kJ by midday. Be in the water by 8am; by 11am it is over.

dee-why.window: 7:30am–11am. Peak 252 kJ at 10am on a light SE offshore, tide filling toward the mid-morning high. Chest to head — nearly double today's size at the Point.
alerts: 7s spacing — fast, stacked sets rather than clean lines
Energy halves after 11am (252 → 137 kJ by midday)

long-reef.window: 7:30am–11am. Biggest of the four — chest to a foot overhead — with the SE offshore straight on it. The pick of the weekend if you want size.
alerts: Biggest and fastest — 4ft on 7s spacing
Gone by midday

curl-curl.window: 8am–11am. Matches Long Reef for size with slightly more forgiving banks on a SE angle. North end first.
alerts: Closeout risk on the bigger sets at 7s
Energy drops away sharply from 11am

manly.window: 8am–11am. Smallest of the four again but the SE angle reaches it far better than today's south — actually rideable, unlike Saturday.
alerts: Still the smallest of the four
Wind goes cross-shore mid-afternoon

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Two very different days. Saturday is small and weak in the morning (90 kJ at 10am) and only fills in once the S cross-shore is on it — a 11am–1pm consolation session at Curl Curl or Long Reef at best. Sunday is the day: 239 kJ at 8am peaking at 252 kJ by 10am with a light SE offshore holding, Long Reef running chest to a foot overhead and Curl Curl not far behind. Both days are rated poor–fair by Surfline because the swell is short-period windswell, not groundswell, but Sunday has nearly twice the energy and the better wind. Take Sunday 8–11am and treat Saturday as optional.

dee-why.window: Sun 7:30am–11am is the weekend session here. Saturday is waist-to-chest on a dead-south 184° — technically surfable, not worth the drive.
alerts: Sat: 184° dead south, small until midday
Sun: peak 252 kJ at 10am, then halves by noon

long-reef.window: Sun 7:30am–11am — biggest surf and best wind of the weekend in one window. Saturday 10am–1pm is the backup if you cannot get out Sunday.
alerts: Sun: 4ft on 7s — fast and stacked
Both days over by early afternoon

curl-curl.window: Sun 8am–11am. Also the best Saturday option (waist to head, 11am–1pm) — the only spot that holds decent size on both days.

manly.window: Sun 8am–11am only. Saturday it is thigh-to-stomach and rated poor from 1pm — write it off.
